title: Add Dedicated tier baseline perf-canary scenario (prompt length dist + concurrency) with regression thresholds
author: Omar El-Sayed
release_notes: Adds a new perf-canary scenario aligned to Dedicated tier baseline workloads, including a stable prompt-length distribution + concurrency profile and regression gates for throughput and tail latency.
description:
Context: As part of the Dedicated throughput SLO + tier definitions work, we need a repeatable perf-canary scenario that matches the baseline workload assumptions used to set tier thresholds. Today our canaries are either microbench-style or too synthetic (single prompt size / fixed concurrency), which makes it hard to catch regressions that shift effective tokens/sec under mixed prompt distributions.

This PR adds a new scenario family `dedicated_tier_baseline_v1` with: (1) a prompt length distribution approximating our tier baseline methodology (short/medium/long mix), (2) a fixed concurrency profile designed to stress continuous batching and queueing behavior, and (3) regression thresholds that gate on both throughput and tail-latency deltas.

What’s included: - New scenario config: `scenarios/dedicated_tier_baseline_v1.yaml` (prompt distribution + concurrency + duration + warmup) - New prompt set manifest: `datasets/dedicated_baseline/prompts_manifest.jsonl` (length-bucketed prompts + deterministic sampling) - Runner updates: support for `prompt_length_distribution` and `bucket_weights` in scenario configs, with deterministic seeding and summary emission for “actual realized distribution” - Metrics + assertions: new checks for `effective_output_tokens_per_second`, `p95_ttft_ms`, and `p95_itl_ms` with regression gates:   - Throughput: fail if `effective_output_tokens_per_second` regresses > 5% vs baseline snapshot for the same model + shape   - TTFT (p95): fail if regression > 10% and absolute p95 exceeds scenario guardrail   - ITL (p95): fail if regression > 15% (more tolerant due to variance under decode scheduling changes)

Baseline snapshots: Adds `baselines/dedicated_tier_baseline_v1/*.json` for the current “known good” canary environment (L4 and A100 runners). These are intentionally stored as relative gates; the harness compares current run to the baseline snapshot for the same target.

Operational notes: - Warmup period is excluded from assertions (matches our measurement standard exclusions). - The harness emits the realized prompt distribution and concurrency achieved, and will mark the run “unstable” (non-gating) if it cannot reach >= 90% of target concurrency due to infra limits.

Why these thresholds: We calibrated thresholds using the last ~3 weeks of canary variance on the shared runners and tuned to minimize false positives while still catching meaningful regressions (batching/scheduler changes have historically shifted effective tokens/sec by 8–12% when they go wrong).

Follow-ups (out of scope here): - Add an H100 runner baseline snapshot once fleet capacity is stable in us-east. - Wire scenario results into the Dedicated dashboards (Sergio is tracking via ENG-2201).

Links: - Linear: ENG-2216 (standardize benchmark workloads used for tier baselines) - Project: Dedicated throughput SLO + tier definitions (PM-482)

Test plan: - `make test` (unit tests for scenario parser + assertions) - Ran `./bin/perf-canary run scenarios/dedicated_tier_baseline_v1.yaml --dry-run` locally - Validated canary run on staging runner (A100) and confirmed snapshot generation + gating behavior (see CI artifacts).
commits: perfcanary: add dedicated_tier_baseline_v1 scenario config + docs
assertions: add throughput + tail-latency regression gates (baseline snapshots)
ci: upload scenario summary + baseline comparison artifacts
tests: parser + distribution realization unit coverage
conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): Can you confirm the scenario’s “effective_output_tokens_per_second” matches what runtime exports (decode-only vs prefill+decode)? We need apples-to-apples with the tier baseline work.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Good call. In this harness we define effective_output_tokens_per_second as output tokens / (scenario_time - warmup), including prefill+decode wall time (same as the Dedicated throughput measurement standard draft). I added an explicit note to docs and renamed the internal variable from decode_tok_s to effective_output_tok_s to avoid confusion.
Aisha Bello (review): Regression gates: what happens if the run can’t hit target concurrency? I’m worried we’ll get noisy failures when the runner is constrained.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Agree. Implemented an “unstable run” classification: if achieved_concurrency < 0.9 * target_concurrency, assertions are marked non-gating and CI reports a warning with the reason + achieved numbers. This should keep the canary informative without blocking merges on infra hiccups.
Sergio Costa (review): Please emit the realized prompt bucket histogram in the JSON summary; it’ll help when debugging drift / sampling bugs.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Done. Summary now includes: configured bucket weights, realized histogram (counts + pct), and the RNG seed. Also added a small unit test to ensure the histogram sums to 1.0 within epsilon.

Irene Choi (review): Baselines include L4 and A100. Are we confident these are stable across regions? Also can we keep the baseline file naming consistent with shape IDs used by fleet (e.g., a100-80gb vs a100-40gb)?

Omar El-Sayed (author): Updated baseline filenames to match fleet shape IDs we use in canary runner labels: `a100-80gb.json` and `l4-24gb.json`. Re: region stability—these are runner-specific; the harness keys on runner label + shape so we won’t cross-compare between different environments by accident.
Sofia Ivanova (review): One more: ITL p95 regression tolerance at 15% seems high. Can you justify or add a comment?

Omar El-Sayed (author): Added inline comment: ITL variance is materially higher under decode scheduling changes and network jitter; 10% was causing false positives in trial runs. We can tighten after we’ve run this for a couple weeks and have better variance estimates.
Sergio Costa (review): Looks good. Approved once CI passes.
Aisha Bello (review): Approved. Thanks for adding the unstable-run guard; that’s exactly what we need for paging hygiene later.
Omar El-Sayed (author): CI is green now. Squashing and merging.
